title: Kepler Q1 to Q16 do not resolve excess core-tail covariance over phase controls in KOI-2700
abstract: We test whether the core and tail losses of KOI-2700 vary together within each orbit. Kepler release 25 gives 1245 accepted transit orbits in Q1 to Q16. After propagation of shared-baseline noise, aperture transit covariance is 86721 ppm squared. Before and after controls give 71277 and 120376. The excess is -9105, with a conditional 95 percent block interval of -50465 to 22673. Corrected flux gives an excess of 3449, with interval -11860 to 17567. A quadratic baseline sharply reduces covariance but gives no stable positive excess. Contrast-space injections and arithmetic checks pass. Positive within-transit covariance alone does not establish dust-supply changes in this test. Correlated noise, phase controls, selection, and source confusion limit inference. No new planet or physical signal is confirmed. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, exact input hashes and an external retrieval recipe are included.

display.caption: Core-tail covariance after shared-baseline noise correction, with conditional 95 percent block intervals. Off-transit controls have comparable covariance.
